prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of one floor of a dreamlike dungeon at the bottom of oblivion in a fantasy JRPG world as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted colour ramps, dark warm outlines, clean readable detail), classic top-down RPG map view seen from above with a slight 3/4 tilt (tree crowns, rocks and buildings seen from above with their south-facing sides visible; NOT an isometric view, NOT a diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render, no perspective).

THE PLACE: THE SECOND DEPTH OF OBLIVION, THE STITCHED WOOD: three remembered landscapes torn out of other lands, floating as islands in a bottomless sea of soft pale grey-violet mist: a green FOREST GLADE with leafy trees in the north-west, a pale DESERT of rippled sand with a few low sandstone rocks in the south-west, a SNOWFIELD of clean snow with snow-laden pines in the east. Their outer edges are torn like the edges of paper. They are joined by long flat bridges made of layered sheets of WHITE PAPER stitched together with dark thread. A white marble staircase going up in the forest (north), a white marble staircase going down in the south of the snowfield. Dreamlike, clean and calm.

The FIRST attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE drawn on a 44 x 34 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output; the output is 2112 x 1632 px). Trace over it: your painting is laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and used directly as the walkable game map, so every road, shore, cliff, wall, tree mass, water body and landmark must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size (keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide; do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep the exact width of the roads and of the one- and two-tile gaps).

The SECOND attached image is only a STYLE REFERENCE from the same game: match its pixel-art rendering (pixel size, clusters, outlines, hue-shifted ramps, level of detail), but use the palette of THE PLACE below. Do NOT copy anything from it (no buildings, piers, water or objects from it).

The guide is soft colour-coding only (its blurred edges only mean the edge is natural and free-flowing): do NOT copy its flat colours, straight tile steps, circles or stripes. Interpret every area as the real material with rich natural variation, and give shores, meadows, rocks and cliffs natural, organic, slightly irregular outlines (bulging or receding by at most a third of a tile around the guide edge). Keep it CLEAN and calm: large readable shapes, smooth even surfaces, no fussy clutter, no scattered debris; a quiet, dreamlike, melancholic place.

Guide colour key:
- pale grey-violet = the VOID (not walkable): a bottomless sea of soft, pale grey-violet MIST seen from above, clearly a little darker and cooler than every walkable ground, calm and almost featureless (only a few faint wisps and a very few small loose white pages drifting in it). Every edge between walkable ground and the void is a clean, crisp, slightly irregular torn edge (like the torn edge of a sheet of paper) with a thin shadow line on the void side, so the walkable shape reads at a glance.
- off-white = fine WHITE SAND that looks like finely shredded paper (walkable, flat, smooth, very little detail).
- light grey with block lines = polished pale IVORY-WHITE MARBLE FLOOR tiles (walkable, flat), clearly paler than the walls.
- green = a soft GRASS meadow of a remembered forest (walkable, flat); dark green circles = leafy TREES packed together (not walkable).
- sand yellow = pale DESERT SAND with soft wind ripples (walkable, flat); grey-brown circles = low sandstone ROCKS (not walkable).
- white = deep clean SNOW (walkable, flat); dark teal circles with white rims = SNOW-LADEN PINES (not walkable).
- dark red = a long faded red CARPET (walkable).
- mid grey with block lines = thick WALLS of cool BLUE-GREY ashlar seen from above (not walkable), their top edge and their south face visible, straight and square.
All walkable areas are LEVEL GROUND.
Landmarks (paint each exactly on its block, at the block's size):
- the blocks in colour rgb(244,242,236) = a long flat BRIDGE of layered sheets of WHITE PAPER stitched together with dark thread, lying over the mist (walkable).
- the blocks in colour rgb(200,196,186) = a white marble STAIRCASE going UP into soft light (walkable).
- the blocks in colour rgb(120,124,150) = a white marble STAIRCASE going DOWN into pale mist (walkable).
Walkable areas must stay walkable-looking: no boulders, trees, fences, crates or objects standing on them unless the guide shows them.

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps. Characters in this game are about 72 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer (the game darkens it into night at runtime and adds lamp light on top). Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light as in the style reference; NO darkness, NO night tint, NO long cast shadows, NO light pools, NO glow halo, NO vignette, NO fog over the map, NO clouds over the map.
Do NOT paint any characters, people, animals, monsters, birds, boats or ships on the water (unless a landmark says so), treasure chests, lanterns, lamp posts, torches, campfires, signs, signposts, text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames or UI. Those are added later as separate sprites: leave the ground open for them.
